hints: Focus on what makes a good preparation of an insoluble salt, precipitation followed by filtration, washing and drying.
Check route 1 first, Ba heated in oxygen gives BaO, which with HCl gives soluble BaCl2, ready to precipitate with sulfate.
Now test routes 2 and 3 for the same pattern, do they both end with a soluble barium compound mixing with dilute H2SO4 to give insoluble BaSO4?
walkthrough:
**Recall the rule for BaSO4**

Barium sulfate is insoluble in water. The pure dry solid is best made by precipitating it from a soluble barium salt, then filtering, washing and drying.

$$\text{soluble Ba}^{2+}(aq) + \text{SO}_4^{2-}(aq) \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4(s)$$

**Check route 1**

Ba in oxygen gives barium oxide, then HCl gives soluble barium chloride, then H2SO4 precipitates BaSO4.

$$\text{Ba} + \tfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{BaO}$$
$$\text{BaO} + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{BaCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{BaCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4 + 2\text{HCl}$$

**Check route 2**

Strong heating of barium nitrate gives BaO as the solid product. Dissolving in excess water gives soluble Ba(OH)2, then H2SO4 precipitates BaSO4.

$$2\text{Ba(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{BaO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$
$$\text{BaO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Ba(OH)}_2$$
$$\text{Ba(OH)}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Check route 3 and conclude**

Ba(OH)2 with dilute HNO3 gives soluble barium nitrate, then H2SO4 precipitates BaSO4.

$$\text{Ba(OH)}_2 + 2\text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow \text{Ba(NO}_3)_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{Ba(NO}_3)_2 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4 + 2\text{HNO}_3$$
All three routes end with filtration, washing and drying of the precipitate, so all three give pure BaSO4.

options.A: Correct. Routes 1, 2 and 3 all produce a soluble Ba2+ solution just before the final step, then precipitate BaSO4 with dilute H2SO4. Filtering, washing and drying gives a pure sample in each case.
options.B: Incorrect. This option includes only routes 1 and 2. Route 3 is also valid because Ba(OH)2 plus HNO3 gives soluble Ba(NO3)2, which precipitates pure BaSO4 with H2SO4.
options.C: Incorrect. This option omits route 1. Route 1 is valid because BaO plus HCl gives soluble BaCl2, which is an ideal precursor for BaSO4 precipitation.
options.D: Incorrect. This option suggests only route 1 works. Routes 2 and 3 also work because thermal decomposition followed by dissolving, and neutralisation to the nitrate, both give soluble barium reagents that precipitate BaSO4 cleanly.
